concerns.quote: There was no check to ensure that the communication was effective between the two groups in their final resting positions
concerns.hazard: ineffective communication between cadets and staff

concerns.quote: The new policy in place dealing with communication checks- Air Cadet Fieldcraft Training Instruction Number 7 -Improvised Camping in a Field Environment, remains unclear in relation to communication checks
Instructors therefore should be directed to ensure that effective communications exist between cadets and supervising staff before the 2 groups retire at night

reports.title: Benjamin McQueen: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Accident at Work and Health and Safety related deaths

promises.quote: Carrying spare breathing apparatus cylinders in safety boats in addition to those carried by the stand-by diver where this is practicable
promises.summary: Carry spare breathing apparatus cylinders in safety boats

promises.quote: When SCADE is employed by the standby diver within un-marked swimming operations, consideration within the Dive Project Plan / Risk Assessment must be given as to the availability of a second Diving Life Support Equipment (DLSE) at immediate notice
promises.summary: Require second DLSE availability in dive risk assessments

promises.quote: Training establishments understand that safety critical training must not be accelerated or truncated solely to accommodate visits by VIPs or senior ranking Officers
promises.summary: Prohibit acceleration of safety-critical training for VIP visits

promises.quote: The use of defibrillators in drowning casualties must balance any potential benefit against the risk of harm
promises.summary: Review defibrillator risk assessment criteria for diving

concerns.quote: A stand-by diver was present at the dive exercise and he was deployed to try to find and rescue Ben. However, the stand-by diver had to surface having run out of breathable gas before Ben was found. A spare breathing apparatus cylinder was not carried in the safety boat for the stand-by diver (or other divers) to use in the event that the stand-by diver's main cylinder ran out.
concerns.hazard: stand-by diver ran out of breathable gas

concerns.quote: The progression of the dive training in which Ben was engaged was safety-critical. The progression of training was accelerated for several reasons, one of which was a visit by a high-ranking naval officer. The concern of the instructing staff was to polish the drills ahead of that visit and to take the pressure off the dive students by allowing them to practise the dive with relevant equipment ahead of the visit. This acceleration of safety-critical training in part because of such a visit was not appropriate.

Ben was lifted unconscious from the sea bed and Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation was immediately started. A defibrillator was also applied, but this was only available because it was carried by a Harbour Patrol vessel which came to assist. I am concerned that in such safety-critical military diving training, the dive support staff did not have available to them a defibrillator of their own either on the supporting safety boats or on land. This did not cause or contribute to Ben's death but could lead to future fatalities.

There is an inconsistency regarding the minimum safety pressure level for the relevant diver's breathing apparatus as between the maintenance manual for which DE&S is responsible and all other policy and safety guidance.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the absence of a defibrillator/AED during military training activities where prompt cardiac resuscitation could be life‑saving. The settings differ (cadet fieldcraft versus military diving), but the specific hazard is the same.
